title.note: Game title kept in English (glossary: keep; no Finnish title supplied).

hud.cast.note: heittää = cast the line, the everyday fishing verb.

hud.reel.note: kelata = reel the line in; the pass name Automaattikela uses the same root.

hud.bait_left.note: Label form: '{count} syöttiä' would show '1 syöttiä' when count is 1.

catch.success.note: 'Sait...' would need the object ending -n on both inserted words. The anglers' idiom 'jäädä saaliiksi' keeps {rarity} and {fish} in base form, so 'Saaliiksi jäi Myyttinen Lyhtyankerias!' agrees for any tier and fish. Inserted words stay capitalized (accepted game style).
catch.success.blind_remark: with the inserted labels the words appear capitalized mid-sentence, e.g. "Myyttinen Kultakarppi"

catch.escaped.note: Names the fish with the generic word; a bare 'Se' reads vague in a toast.

catch.new_record.note: For the developer: Finnish writes decimals with a comma (12,4 kg); {weight} arrives as 12.4, so format it per locale in code.

fish.lantern_eel.note: lyhty (lantern) + ankerias (eel), one compound. Real lanternfish are 'lyhtykalat' in Finnish, so the coinage reads natural and keeps the glowing-lantern idea.

rarity.mythic.note: Tier above Legendaarinen (the guide's Legendary). Nominative adjective, so it works inserted before {fish}.

shop.rods.note: vapa = fishing rod, plural vavat; not 'tangot' (metal rods).

shop.equip.note: Button verb as the guide uses it ('Varusta {pet} -lemmikki'); pairs with the state label 'Käytössä'.

shop.equipped.note: 'In use': the usual Finnish state label. 'Varustettu' also fits but sounds stiffer.

shop.buy_robux.note: The guide's 'Osta {price} Robuxilla' is the most natural Finnish, but lint's keep-term check rejects the inflected 'Robuxilla' (it needs 'Robux' with no letter after it). The price sits in parentheses as a price tag, where the bare unit reads fine for any price. If the developer relaxes that check for Finnish, switch to 'Osta {price} Robuxilla'.

pass.auto_reel.note: 'Automatic reel' (the device), same root as Kelaa. 14/14; 'Automaattikelaus' (16) is over budget. The Creator Hub pass name should match.

pass.lucky_bait.note: Onnensyötti = onni (luck) + syötti (bait), one compound like 'Onnenjuoma'. Tags stay around the pass name.

sell.done.note: '{count} kalaa' and '{coins} kolikkoa' would show '1 kalaa', '1 kolikkoa'. Genitive '{count} kalan saaliin' (a catch of N fish) and the adessive price '{coins} kolikolla' are correct for 1 and every other number.

sell.prompt.note: Guide's '-malla' pattern ('Avaa painamalla E'); E kept.

ascend.button.note: kohota = rise to a higher level. Not religious ('ylösnousemus') and not 'get up' or climbing, as 'Nouse' would read. No established Finnish word for this mechanic; native check welcome. Alternative: 'Ylennys' (promotion).

ascend.confirm.text: Haluatko kohota nyt? Aloitat alusta, mutta saat harvinaisia kaloja {bonus} % useammin.
ascend.confirm.note: Same verb as ascend.button. Finnish writes a space before % (25 %). 'saada kalaa' is the everyday 'catch fish'.

weather.storm.text: Myrsky on tulossa! Harvinaiset kalat tärppäävät.
weather.storm.note: tärpätä = a fish takes the bait, the word Finnish anglers and kids use; 'syövät' would read as just eating.

quest.catch_n.note: 'Nappaa {n} kalaa' would show '1 kalaa' when n is 1, so the count moves after a colon, a common quest-line form. Kuutamolahti = Moonlit Bay (kuutamo = moonlight); 'Kuutamolahdella' = at the bay.

friends.boost.note: Space before % per Finnish convention; 'kaverit' per the guide; 'onnea' is the partitive of onni (luck), as in Onnensyötti.

trade.sent.note: Head noun 'pelaajalle' takes the ending so {player} stays in base form. 'lähti' (went out) is the natural toast verb and fits 33, where 'lähetetty' would be 34.

trade.accept.note: {player} is the subject in base form; Finnish past tense has no gender. 'your trade' = your trade request.

afk.kicked.text: Olit liian kauan toimettomana, joten kalastus pysähtyi.
afk.kicked.note: 'joten' (so) carries the cause the context gives; no mention of leaving the server, as in the source.

settings.sfx.note: The usual settings term in Finnish software and games; 'Ääniefektit' is also common.

event.ends.note: 14/14; 'päästä' after a duration needs no ending on {time}. Shorter fallback: 'Jäljellä {time}'. For the developer: {time} arrives as '2d 4h' with English letters; Finnish writes '2 pv 4 t'.
event.ends.blind_remark: "päästä" needs {time} in the genitive, e.g. "5 minuutin"; reads wrong if {time} is a plain form like "5 minuuttia"

daily.streak.text: {day}. päivä putkeen! Palaa huomenna hakemaan lisää.
daily.streak.note: Ordinal '{day}.' ('3. päivä') reads right for every day number, including 1; 'putkeen' (in a row) is the everyday streak word.

tip.night.text: Vinkki: jotkin kalat tärppäävät vain öisin.
tip.night.note: Same 'tärpätä' (bite) as weather.storm; lowercase after the colon.

group.join.text: Liity ryhmäämme, niin saat 50 ilmaista syöttiä!
group.join.note: 'ryhmä' as fi.wikipedia and the guide use it; 'ryhmäämme' (our group) is how Finnish invites phrase it. The fixed 50 takes the partitive correctly.

leaderboard.biggest.note: The board ranks the heaviest single fish; 'Suurin saalis' could read as the biggest total haul.
